title.narrative: Women in Coffee and Food Security for Economic Development

description.narrative: Isebwe Coffee Marketing Cooperative, a women-led smallholder organisation in the Mt. Rwenzori region, is implementing the Women in Coffee, Food Security and Economic Development (WICOFED) project to address long-standing barriers faced by women coffee farmers. Although women contribute most of the labour, they continue to experience limited land ownership, restricted control over income, and low participation in decision-making. These gender inequalities are compounded by low productivity, ageing coffee trees, limited access to inputs, weak post-harvest handling, climate pressures, and dependence on middlemen who suppress farm-gate prices. The WICOFED project seeks to strengthen Isebwe into a competitive, gender-responsive agribusiness. It will equip women and youth with agronomic skills, inputs, and organisational capacity to improve yields, produce specialty coffee, and access higher-value markets. The project will further promote climate-smart practices, diversify household incomes, and enhance food security through integrated cropping systems. Expected results include increased productivity, higher earnings for women, stronger cooperative governance, and more resilient livelihoods across the Mt. Rwenzori coffee belt. Lunar Coffee Ltd., a private company, is engaged separately to provide consultancy-based capacity building for agronomists supporting farmers in good agronomic practices and coffee quality control. Its budget is reflected within the Isebwe project, as the cooperative supplies part of Lunar's coffee.
